groups.olmocr-p001:
VERDICT: The high CER on olmocr_2502.18443_p001 comes from the reference, but not from the title/author/affiliation block. That block's text-layer order matches the page; its only defect is that the ♥ core-contributor markers are missing, which costs models 3-4 chars. The real cause is Figure 1 (the 'Prompt with document anchoring -> Original PDF file -> Generated Markdown file' illustration). Its internal vector text is in the text layer:
- It makes up 1103 of 3225 normalized reference chars (34.2%) and 152 of 468 words.
- It is in panel-interleaved order: the mini-PDF panel comes first, and it is partly hidden under the semi-transparent prompt box. The table comes before 'Section 6', then the prompt box, then the markdown panel.
- It is itself corrupted: monospace spaces are lost ('loremipsumdolorsitamet', 'nostrudexercitationullamcolaborisnisi'), words are split ('s eddo', 'veni am'), and 'Lorem ipsum' appears three times.

FLOOR/CEILING PROOF: I built a figure-stripped reference, work/olmocr_p001_ref_nofig.txt, with the project's own metrics.normalize and jiwer. Against the full reference, a flawless transcription of all non-figure text scores CER 0.342 and word_f1 0.806. That is the floor for any figure-skipping model, and 20 of the 27 units sit within about ±0.04 of it. Even an idealized visual-order transcription that includes all figure text scores CER 0.176 against the full reference; the figure segment alone scores 0.514. Word_f1 on the full reference is also contaminated: a figure-skipping transcription tops out at 0.806, so the spread from 0.72 to 0.83 is not a quality ranking.

REAL MODEL DIFFERENCES, from rescoring against the figure-stripped reference (work/olmocr_p001_rescored.json). Mean figure-stripped CER / word_f1 across 3 levels:
- paddleocr-vl 0.011 / 0.964
- nanonets-ocr2-3b 0.013 / 0.990
- qwen3.5-4b 0.014 / 0.985
- qwen3-vl-4b 0.021 / 0.984
- qwen3-vl-8b 0.035 / 0.981
- olmocr-2-7b 0.070 / 0.961 ('oImOCR' misread x8 at clean; ```yaml front matter leak at light/heavy)
- glm-ocr 0.180 / 0.912 (drops title, authors, affiliation and links at every level; clean and light outputs are byte-identical)
- qwen3.5-9b 0.205 (median 0.053; driven by light, which moved the figure after the abstract as a fabricated table with an invented caption/note)
- qwen3-vl-2b 0.386 (median 0.155; clean hit a runaway '## Contact [https://github.com/AllenAI](http://www.huggin)ing' loop, finish_reason=length at 4096 tokens)

The only real failures on this page are glm-ocr (systematic omission), qwen3-vl-2b clean (loop), qwen3.5-9b light (figure restructuring) and, to a lesser degree, olmocr-2-7b. The others are all near-perfect (figure-stripped CER ≤ 0.055).

RECOMMENDATION: Exclude this page from the headline CER, or rescore it against a figure-masked reference, and report it separately as a 'figure with embedded text' diagnostic. Reasons:
1. It adds about 0.34 CER to every model almost uniformly, which inflates absolute numbers and compresses real differences.
2. It supplies 27 of the 44 outlier units (61%) in the synthetic index.
3. It rewards accidents and punishes fidelity. qwen3-vl-8b clean and qwen3.5-4b clean land below the floor (0.324 and 0.321) because unclosed alt text or figure labels happen to match reference words. The one model that tried to transcribe the figure (qwen3.5-9b light) gets the worst non-loop CER, 0.712.

If a single headline number must include it, use the figure-stripped reference. Longer term, the reference builder should drop text-layer spans inside figure bounding boxes. This figure is vector graphics, not an image, so it needs a drawing-cluster bbox or a manual per-page exclusion.

NORMALIZER GAPS FOUND (apply benchmark-wide):
(a) _MD_IMAGE requires '(src)', so an unclosed '![alt]' leaks model-written alt text into the scored text (qwen3-vl-2b clean/light, qwen3-vl-8b clean). Suggested pattern: '!\[[^\]]*\](\([^)]*\))?'.
(b) Markdown link targets '[text](url)' are kept, so invented URLs are scored (qwen3-vl-8b light, qwen3.5-9b heavy).
(c) olmOCR YAML front matter inside a ```yaml fence is not stripped (olmocr-2-7b light/heavy here); check other pages for the same leak.
(d) The page number '1' is glued to the footer link line, so strip_furniture does not remove it (1 char, negligible).

Scratch files are in <local scratch dir>/failures/work/: olmocr_p001.png, olmocr_p001_fig_zoom.png, olmocr_p001_ref_nofig.txt, olmocr_p001_ref_figure_only.txt, olmocr_p001_ideal_figure.txt, olmocr_p001_rescored.json, metr.py (loads metrics.py without writing bytecode).

9 units (qwen3-vl-2b: 5, 4b: 2, 8b: 2; olmocr p001 excluded). There are two distinct failure types.

(1) All three CER=1.0 cases are repetition loops that run into the 4096-token cap. The units are 2b paperqa2_p001_heavy, 4b paperqa2_p003_heavy and 4b paperqa2_p007_heavy. Telemetry for all three shows gen_tokens=4096, finish_reason=length, and 108 s, 217 s and 203 s wall time, against 8-28 s for their siblings. None of them is an empty output, a refusal or the wrong page's content. CER reads 1.0 only because the scorer caps it: loop insertions make the hypothesis 2.4 to 6.6 times longer than the reference (22.7k vs 3.5k, 20.3k vs 5.9k, 13.8k vs 5.8k chars).
- Two loop shapes appear. 2b finishes the whole page and then restarts the 1.5k-char Introduction block 14 times. 4b gets stuck on a single 124- or 131-char sentence and repeats it about 118 and 76 times.
- Before the loop, the transcription is accurate. With the repeats removed, CER is 0.130, 0.040 and 0.248, and the prefix before the loop in p007 scores 0.007. The p007 figure stays at 0.248 because the loop used up the budget before the last 27% of the page (1,553 chars) was emitted, so it is also a truncation. The 2b case also silently drops the author/affiliation block that its clean sibling kept.
- Every loop happens at the heavy level. The clean/light siblings of the same model and page stopped normally with CER at or below 0.05, and 8b never looped on these pages. So the loops come from small models meeting heavy degradation.
- These outputs are not acceptable for RAG as they stand, because the repeated text would produce duplicate junk chunks and p007 loses content. Fixes on the decode side: a repetition penalty or no_repeat_ngram setting, loop detection with early stop, and dropping repeated paragraphs or sentences afterwards.

(2) The other 6 units (2b attention p001 at all three levels, 2b p004_heavy, 8b p001 clean/light) are not recognition failures. word_f1 is between 0.925 and 0.977, and the high CER comes from where whole blocks were placed.
- 2b rearranges the p001 title page into a template: title, abstract, then invented '## Authors' and '## Footnote' sections. It also omits the red Google permission notice. Putting the blocks back in page order brings CER from 0.345 to 0.068, and restoring the notice brings it to 0.0096.
- 8b puts the ∗†‡ author footnotes before the abstract. That is visually wrong but has a semantic reason: the footnotes annotate the author block. Putting them back after the abstract brings CER from 0.5955 to 0.0032. The behaviour is not stable: 8b read the heavy variant of the same page in correct order (CER 0.0039).
- 2b p004_heavy puts the Figure 2 caption after the body text, a defensible float placement, and drops one carry-over sentence plus one panel label. Fixing both brings CER from 0.18 to 0.011.

In every case I checked the reference against the rendered page and it follows visual order, so none of these is a reference_artifact.

Two smaller issues. A leftover '```markdown' fence puts the word 'markdown' into the scored text; the cost is negligible. And a single block swap of about 1k chars costs 0.3 to 0.6 CER. The benchmark should therefore report word_f1 and char3_f1 next to CER, and separate capped-1.0 loop outputs from genuinely bad transcriptions.

Evidence scripts are in <local scratch dir>/failures/work/: loopcheck.py, sentloop.py, qwen3vl_reorder_att1.py, qwen3vl_p004.py and qwen3vl_p007.py. They use qmetrics.py, a copy of the benchmark's metrics.py. The page renders are att_p001.png and att_p004.png in the same folder.
groups.others:
8 outlier units in this group (6 candidates, excluding olmocr_2502.18443_p001*). Only 3 of them are real content loss or corruption. The rest are page layout choices where the text itself is right.

1) Reading-order and layout choices, text nearly perfect after fixing (4 units)
- qwen3.5-4b att_p001_clean: 0.339 → 0.004 after moving the author block back and adding the permission notice.
- olmocr-2-7b att_p001_light: 0.607 → 0.005 after moving the footnotes back and adding the venue line.
- olmocr-2-7b att_p004_clean/light: 0.22 → 0.032 after moving footnote 4 back to the page end.
- In all of these, CER counts moved blocks at about 2x their length. word_f1 stays at 0.92–0.95. All four are fine for RAG.
- All are stochastic: the same model scores ≤0.075 on at least one other degradation level of the same page.

2) Real failures, not acceptable for RAG (3 units)
- paddleocr-vl att_p008_light: made-up table numbers, a repeated 'IN THEteNet', and paraphrased prose with wrong facts ('3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs' → '15 min for each group', 41.0 → 14.0). Its clean run scored 0.041.
- glm-ocr att_p010_clean: Table 4 silently dropped. CER is 0.0004 on the rest of the page.
- olmocr-2-7b pq_p011_heavy: output is only the YAML front matter (34 tokens, finish_reason=stop). Telemetry flags empty=false, so it is not caught as empty.

3) Invented trailer (1 unit, fine for RAG after filtering)
- qwen3.5-9b pq_p001_light adds a made-up 'References: [Reference 1..8] / Contact / Date / End of Document' section. Without it CER is 0.004. The heavy run of the same page shows the same behavior.

4) olmocr-2-7b formatting-residue check, recomputed over all 36 synthetic units with the benchmark's own reference build and normalizer; this reproduces every official CER exactly
- **YAML front matter:** 15 of 36 outputs start with a front-matter block ('```markdown'/'```yaml' + '---' + 'primary_language: ... is_diagram: ...' + '---'). normalize() drops the backticks and '---' but keeps 'markdown/yaml primarylanguage: en isrotationvalid: true ...' (about 100 chars). That adds a mean of 0.019 CER per affected unit. The model's mean CER goes from 0.1018 to 0.0941 when the block is stripped. None of olmocr's outliers is driven mainly by it; it is the whole failure only in pq_p011_heavy.
- **HTML tables:** there are none in olmocr-2-7b's synthetic outputs, so they inflate nothing. `<sup>` (4 outputs) is already neutralized.
- **Footnotes:** the costly convention is `\footnote{...}` (3 outputs), which moves footnote text to its anchor. It explains about 0.18 of the 0.22 CER on att_p004. The normalizer also leaves the 'footnote' command name behind as a token.
- **Figure labels:** olmocr skips text inside figures (att_p004 'Scaled Dot-Product Attention Multi-Head Attention', 47 chars), a small omission.
- **Suggested normalizer fixes** (outside this group's scope): strip a leading front-matter block and code fences in plain_text(); drop OTSL tokens (<lcel>/<fcel>/<ucel>/<xcel>/<nl>, seen in paddleocr-vl); count front-matter-only output as empty. Also consider an order-tolerant headline metric, or segment alignment, because single-block moves dominate these outliers.

Scratch scripts are in <local scratch dir>/failures/work/: diag.py, whatif.py, w_*.py and allunits.py (full recompute plus the front-matter ablation).
